text:
mel: Hey team — running into a weird client-side repro with the JS sample app. After an auth token rotation the paginator issues the same page fetch twice and our local semaphore gives the permit back twice, which then lets a burst of requests through and we hit soft-429s from the API.

mel: Minimal stack: sample-app -> sdk-js v0.9.3 -> internal prefetch paginator + leaky permit on refresh. Happens on startup under load.

jess: ugh. do we have logs showing duplicate request IDs or just same cursor payload?

mel: logs show identical cursor tokens in the two POSTs, same body, different X-Request-Id headers. Attached snippet below.

mel: ```
POST /v1/paginate
body: { cursor: "c_abc123", page_size: 50 }
headers: { Authorization: Bearer <rotated>, X-Request-Id: r1 }
...
POST /v1/paginate
body: { cursor: "c_abc123", page_size: 50 }
headers: { Authorization: Bearer <rotated>, X-Request-Id: r2 }
```

taylor: Is the SDK calling refreshToken() concurrently for inflight requests? If refresh returns a new token promise but code branch that releases semaphore runs in both inflight paths that would leak permits.

mel: Exactly. Repro steps: 1) simulate expired token mid-prefetch, 2) trigger 3 parallel cursor advances, 3) watch permits go +2 unexpectedly and subsequent window bursts.

omar: Has anyone tried on go/python sdk? Might be js-only due to how our mutex around token refresh is implemented in js-sdk v0.9.x.

jess: I can confirm node sampleapp on my laptop shows same behavior with 100 concurrent clients. We should add a test that asserts semaphore count after refresh.

taylor: Proposed quick patch: ensure refreshToken() is singleflight (share promise) AND ensure semaphore.release() happens only in the success/finalizer for the owner that actually consumed the permit. Pseudocode: 

```
// tokenManager.js
if (!refreshing) { refreshing = refresh(); }
await refreshing; // others await same promise
// only call release if you previously acquired and did NOT requeue
```

mel: Also thinking: we should fail-fast duplicate cursor requests client-side by deduping by (cursor, inflightKey) for a short window (50ms). Might prevent double-sends during rotation.

omar: That helps but feels like a bandaid. Root is concurrency around auth + permit lifecycle. SDK parity note: go/python semaphores behave differently because their token manager uses a lock, not promise-sharing. We should document parity gap and add test matrix.

jess: I'll open a PR with two commits: 1) add singleflight token refresh util + unit tests, 2) tighten semaphore ownership semantics + add integration test in sampleapp harness.

mel: Thanks! Can we also add a sampleapp config flag to intentionally rotate tokens every N seconds so CI can catch regressions?

taylor: good idea. @deploy-bot can we run a quick canary on staging after merge?
deploy-bot: deploy job queued for staging/sdks-sampleapp (canary). ETA ~8m :rocket:

jess: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/842 (draft). Tests added, still running flaky prefetch scenario.

mel: Awesome. After this lands we should also add a short doc blurb in devex/README about auth/retry ordering and semaphore expectations so integrators understand why leases must be released exactly once.

omar: I'll draft the doc. TL;DR: "Do not release client-side permits from both the retry branch and the success branch — own the permit until work is complete or explicitly requeue."

taylor: :thumbsup: Once PR merges let's run the load test used in repro and mark this resolved.

mel: Thanks all, saved us from a surprise 429 wave in staging.
